reviews.text: 今天90块买的战锤3，70块买的索尼克，不到600M的地牢3卖我64，但是我就要玩，好玩爱玩

如果你是奔着地牢战争2的遗物刷取来的，那我可以直接告诉你，别买地牢战争3.第三代删除了遗物刷取以及天赋系统，取代而之的是一个最大插槽为8的符印栏，然后你需要用关卡里刷出的灵魂碎片去商店购买毫无新意且数值蚊子腿的符印。这些符印能给你带来什么呢？百分之三十的仆从血量，敌人收到伤害增加百分之十，敌人护甲减半这种纯粹的数值加强。不像地牢战争2还可以打怪爆出例如血量翻倍，陷阱等级增加，伤害倍率这种有意思的遗物。陷阱有很多新类型，但也做了非常多的负优化，原本升级在固定的三个升级里选一个。现在升级在场外选一个选好然后一条路走到死。地图从以前的走格子加随机生成地图变成了拼格子加（可能是手作地图），最恶心的是什么呢，地图至少在前期是线性的，你只有一关一关的闯才能解锁后面的内容，而不是像前代一样打不过这关可以打另一关。地图难度也极高，你要是前期想加点铭文增加经验，那你就会像我一样在琢磨如何推进的时候错过退款时间。对这代作品，我是非常非常失望的，我在游戏刚发售的后一分钟买入游戏，因为前作的有趣让我毫不犹豫，但现在毫无疑问失去了前作特色的本作是纯纯的一坨。

与前作的体验有较大差别。前期难度应该比前作高，玩得有点难受。没有天赋了，取而代之的是有增益的地块，每过一关给你发一些地块进行摆放和一次撤销地块的机会。关卡内不会随机掉落遗物和难度符文，并且难度符文只有固定的选项。遗物需要在商店使用灵魂碎片购买(!最重量级的是陷阱格子和遗物格子都需要花灵魂碎片!)，一些特殊地块也能在商店购买，灵魂碎片在基础难度中不会掉落，需要选择难度符文（意味着你每次获得新的难度符文都要重复刷，难度符文有经验可以升级），前期刷一次也就一两百，但是遗物价格普遍较高，更别说你可能还要开格子。关卡内不能随意更换陷阱的升级选项，好像需要地块靠近图书馆地块才可以随意选（我一开始还以为放了图书馆就能随意升级了）。

To say this is imbalanced is an understatement. I'm at Flooded digsite (after 10 ish maps ) and this map is pure torture. none of your traps do enough damage not ven when fully upgraded and after wave 4 !!! x 40 balloons come flying trough... It's terrible man. I don't even think this map is clearable with the recources i have.. I'm at my 20th try or so , Have respecced numerous times, tried different combo's but no... They don't give us enough damage, they don't give us enough cash, u only get 50 gold for pushing a wave instead of 150 so it's not even worth it. Not even is it not worth it but its impossible to clear for the 50 extra gold. I HAVE freaking 4 !! trap slots and I've been playing since launch. Is that also too much too ask??? Also it's literally impossible to clear all the objectives on the former maps because it asks me to clear it with runes i don't even have !!... What's the idea of this? We can't even farm levels because you won't let us.. For instance: Clear this map with X and Y rune. Sure ... I have X but I don't have Y yets so It's impossible for me to clear the secondary objective... Leaving out precious points that could be used for upgrading traps. it's every freaking map man... Every map has a secondary objective which want you to clear it with1 -4 relics of you you don't own one ore more of them. This is terrible design. I can't level properly if I can't do secondary objectives.... Also nice to give the player only one choice of map everytime. Instead of a choice of maps like in the old one. So if your stuck, you really are stuck... Makes no sense to me. Units have -30 percent heatlth ... yeah right.. -30 percent of infinity is still infinity. This early t2 map feels like a t12 in the former game. It's insane. Do I need to buy the dlc for more then 4 trap slots? Is clearing 12 maps not good enough ? Wth is this stingy business ? Edit: The devs have taken full responsability and are trying to iron most of these issue's out, they have already released 4 patches , in the 4 days that it's out. So I will keep this review updated. So far I haven't changed my mind.

Played the demo for a few hours. Love dungeon warfare games, best tower defense imop, looking forward to a may-or-maynot 3d coop version that was teased in passing. However this game feels like a weird off-brand, nothing that worked in the previous games works here, even micro-managing and min-maxing a strat from the previous game barely lets you win here, if even then. Never was a huge fan of the map-rng system, its cool in look, but execution feels... odd. Difficulty was skyrocketed out of nowhere, don't get me wrong I like a challenge, but on the 3rd map, having to sell towers the last few mobs bypassed to build ahead just not to lose is a bit ridiculous. Think bloon td 6 impossible difficulty without the towers unlocked or upgrades unlocked yet. Plus another nitpick that's never be QOL'd out is the placeable consumable traps, you have to baby sit it and not forget it exists or you're at a disadvantage, I don't know why they don't just let it stack a few times in case you forget the crappy things even exist. Willing to change my review if they post-release polish it a bit, but right now I cannot really play the way I want to anymore.
物品解锁和商店价格很坐牢，导致前期缺乏正反馈，再玩玩看。不理解下本为什么只能带一种路线，大大降低了自由度。
Game is no longer fun.

作为2代来的玩家，有点失望。 游戏从2代极具特点的刷爆塔防降级为了一般塔防，放弃自身深度刷爆的特色，如今有点泯然众人的味道。 美术和表现也没有很大革新，如果后续更新有优化才能推荐 如果是从没接触该系列的新玩家【推荐】 如果是2代老玩家【不推荐】 As a player from the 2nd generation, I’m somewhat disappointed. The game has been downgraded from the highly distinctive loot-heavy tower defense of the 2nd installment to a generic tower defense experience, abandoning its deep and engaging特色. Now it feels rather mediocre. The art and presentation also lack significant innovation. I’d only recommend it if future updates bring improvements. If you’re new to the series — 【Recommended】 If you’re a veteran of the 2nd game — 【Not Recommended】
前作好玩的无限提升和有趣的遗物系统没有了，加入了完全意义不明随机地块效果和极度限制玩家性能的符文系统，新塔除了激光都缺乏新意和强度，旧塔也改的一塌糊涂，防御塔升级大多还是无脑加数值缺乏质变，白白期待好几年还不如前作

在制作组能自己开荒不刷刷刷一次性打完静谧（第四波开始刷出一大堆的黑色骑士）和挖掘地（第三波刷出三个攻城车）的无暇前，我选择给差评。 1.04版本补充：官方把黑色骑士的免伤从幽默的20次砍成了10次，现在的难度开荒应该算是能打的了。挖掘地的刷怪波次官方也说进行了调整，但是第三波的三个面包车依旧还在，调整了个寂寞。对于中期部分过难的关卡，官方给出的解决方案是多了一些新手关卡来给玩家过渡刷经验。但是新加的关卡完全没有支线奖励，就只给了通关经验和3红钻。和让玩家去开符文刷前面的关卡拿经验这种最原始的解决方法相比没好到哪去。还是希望可以在新手图里多加点成长补强。 首先是塔的专精升级不再提供冷却时间减少。而玩家也没有了科技和遗物的被动加成，火力和二代没法比。这系列游戏老玩家都知道只有群体aoe可以用，单体塔是完全上不了场的。拿10级闪电为例是5秒打14伤害，2.8的dps，而我们的攻城车呢？有100血，别说这个面包车里面还有一堆面包人了，成型的阵容甚至都很难打掉面包车的100血。你们挖掘地第三波就刷3个攻城车有自己打过吗？玩家想要打无暇基本就只能亏钱用箱子砸，然后很容易导致后面缺钱输出跟不上。目前游戏里塔的输出和怪物的属性是完全不对等的，也就是大家所说的“难度比前作高”。如果说1 2代是可以花样游玩，刷刷刷后可以无双割草的话，那3就是不回去刷刷刷你连主线都过不去。 地块系统看着非常美好，说是rogue元素，其实也就那样。上限也就是一块地周围围三种buff地形。然后反复的用回收卡来刷每一关。而且稀有的地形卡必须要通过商店才能大量购买，而商店的货币还需要玩家支付1000（更新后是800）货币才能开始无限制少量的刷货币。加上不合理的关卡难度很容易让玩家觉得厌烦。到了后期都买的差不多后又会有饱和的情况，那这部分系统就完全没有了意义。新版本更新后每关初始自带50的货币，也只是杯水车薪。想要财富自由就只能攒钱堆800的建筑。但是货币这部分的增益又带不到飞升后的世界。就导致玩家根本没有反复刷刷刷的欲望。另外关于地形补充点小知识，为了刷征服者等级，经验倍率是很重要的，所以刷关卡的时候山脉的经验buff是必备的。但其实这个经验buff是可以被强化的。如果玩家有山脉周围也都是被山脉包围时，这个山脉会被强化，地图上看着就是中心的山脉图标上的树木会偏黄一些，这个时候这片山脉地形就会被赋予另一个经验buff：山巅。最开始是额外20%，根据强化山脉的数量提升效果，本人最高是到40%，不清楚是不是上限。和山脉的30%加一起就是70%的倍率，很可观了。 然后是塔方面，一大堆的辅助塔和一大堆的单体塔，使得玩家对输出塔的选择变得十分单一，塔和怪物差距过大的数值使得玩家想过关就只能用偏控制的阵容，最后基本就只有火焰（dot和减速）和闪电（眩晕控制）是性价比合格的对群输出了。而且明明1 2代都可以在游戏内自选升级路线，为啥3就要做成开局前绑定一种升级的模式。弃其精华，取之糟粕？如果你为了在无尽模式建立经济基础而给箱子的阶选了炼金，那么正常堵路的箱子就不能被升阶了，因为你只能给堵路的箱子升级成炼金，而炼金是会被主动攻击掉的。同理你也不能用陷阱基座这个3阶升级了。这个改动就很奇怪，我无法理解你们为什么要这么改。另外地刺的2阶升级明明写的是聚拢怪物，却不像黑洞那样，而是会把怪物挤的到处都是，完全就是负面的强化效果。然后是塔的种类方面，大家也都说了，原以为demo里是冰山一角，结果所见即所有，也是让人很失望。 地图内的一些隐藏设计还是很不错的，拆金库和坟墓这些当小支线来玩。但有一部分的渴血方尖碑设计非常不合理，直白点说就是有多个渴血方尖碑的关卡。如果只有一个，玩家可以在方尖碑周围来布防完成条件，但有多个的场合，不是玩家需要多处布防，而是玩家需要把原本的塔全部拆掉换到另一个地方，以防止怪物被之前的陷阱击杀到不了第二个方尖碑处。简单来说就是要亏钱，加上怪物的数值问题，很容易崩盘或者完成不了后续渴血方尖碑的条件需求。这给人的体验是非常差的。 但新加入的KR类似英雄单位还是蛮不错的，但是缺少相关的操作教程,英雄是可以通过左键选中英雄单位或者左下角头像后用右键移动的，游戏里完全没有相关的说明。另外BTD系列的气球彩蛋也依旧还在。希望制作组能把这些问题修复一下，把游戏打磨的更好吧。
A significant downgrade in pretty much every measurable way from DW2. I can't in good conscience suggest you buy this when the prequel is just a better game in every way with more content.

It's got potential, but I've got a couple gripes: - Scaling is off. Endless mode doesn't feel "endless" enough. I want to [i]feel[/i] my progression, not die in 6 waves. - Some of the pre-designed maps just aren't fun to play on. I don't want to write a thesis on maze-building (or the lack-thereof). - The tower unlocks, as they are done now, are not a good mechanic. I believe that the towers should be more key to the level when introduced. As an example, the map flamethrowers are introduced, there's not a great place for them. This is generally the same for all the traps I've unlocked so far.

Solid! Reading other reviews I was expecting massive difficulty spike.... Yea, no. This is a well paced, slow burn type of game. Those expecting to unlock all, and be able to breeze through 100 waves of endless 5 hours in will be disappointed.

A worthy sequel that improved on everything the previous games had to offer, with more unique traps and fun levels. The skill tree was gutted/replaced by a different system and honestly I am okay with that. DW2 had a bit too much RNG in its levels that could make or break a strategy/build, whereas here each trap has 3 set-in-stone items for them that fill a similar lore to the items of DW2, but without the terrible luck factor. We also have sigils that you equip that give various effects that help you out, so we still have a decent amount of customization with how we approach the game. The traps are more fun and they all feel worth using so far, whereas some traps in DW2 were... questionable... The pixel art has only improved, with some really cool effects. Arcane trap, my beloved, you look so cool. There are some brand-new additions, like the way the map works, where you shape the world the way you want and get various effects on the levels which you also choose where to place. Struggling with a level because of enemies with too much armor? Place the dungeon in a wasteland biome and they'll have less. It's an interesting gimmick, and you can always choose to change things around with a limited (but easily acquired) item. We now have Wilson and the Necromancer, a passive, loosely-controlled entity that helps (and taunts) while flying around the dungeon and a more directed stall unit that does okay-ish damage respectively. While I like these features, I think a way to turn them off in the options would be nice for those that want it, as I've seen some people dislike these additions. [strike] The only real criticisms I have for the game are on the UI level rather than the actual gameplay part. I would like there to be some kind of indicator for levels that have been cleared but have an uncompleted secondary objective, (like "survive a wave with wrath level 5), as checking each same-looking tower one by one gets old fast. Similarly, I wish the game told me what those objectives give. I would like to know if I'm going to be getting an upgrade for my favorite trap or if I'm getting a sigil. I went back to complete every objective because a level asked to be completed with a "vine" rune, and I assumed since I have this level asking me for the vine rune, I must have missed it. I did not miss it, and it was a later level that unlocked this instead. Having the information relayed to the player would have been a nice addition. [/strike] Edit: a hotfix added the ability to see what each objective unlocks, so ignore this part of the review :) All in all, I recommend this game, whether you're a fan of DW1 or DW2, or if you're new to the series. (Also shoutouts to Groquest who I've randomly been seeing posting on r/pixelart about the art in this game, it was cool to get a sneakpeak and to see an artist's growth!)
真的很失望，我是一代就入坑的老玩家，也是因为独特的肝装备、遗物才入被吸引进来的，说实话，我真是抱着百分之三百的期待第一时间购入的，心想这下又可以大刷特刷了，但没想到，三代取消了可以刷遗物，无限割草，无限提升的特性，玩了几个小时，实在是玩不下去了，我觉得这真是捡了芝麻丢了西瓜，太失望了。明明这款游戏的基调就是塔防无双，越割越爽，越刷越爽，真的想不通为什么要这样。

Dungeon Warfare 3 is a disappointing sequel to a great franchise, in dungeon warfare 2 there are multiple skill trees you can freely spend points in that can drastically change how you play, in contrast dungeon warfare 3 has a minimal skill system (that I didn't even unlock until after I beat the base story) where skill points only provide slight bonuses to trap cooldown, starting money, etc. The skill system in Dungeon Warfare 3 does not meaningfully change how you play, and is a disappointment compared to 2's system. Additionally 2 had items you could obtain from stages that provided random bonuses, this provided a lot of replayability, farming for new and better items, 3 lacks the item system, meaning once you finish the base story and complete the stage objectives for all of the missions, that's it, there's little else to do in the game. Dungeon Warfare 3 is a fun game, solid 7/10 for me, but it falls leagues short of dungeon warfare 2, so if you haven't played 2 yet, I recommend getting 2 instead of this game.

Dungeon Warfare 3 would have worked well as a standalone title but, as the third part in what is now a trilogy, I can't help but feel it lives in the shadow of its predecessor. I can't recommend Dungeon Warfare 3 when it feels like nothing but a watered-down version of Dungeon Warfare 2 with little more than the addition of a shallow deckbuilding mechanic to entice players. Again, as a standalone title, Dungeon Warfare 3 would be fine. I wouldn't hate the game but I remember how much of a step up the second game felt from the first. This one, while unique, feels like it's taking a step back down, like they tacked on the previously mentioned deckbuilding mechanic to the first game and called it a day. I find it hard to see Dungeon Warfare 3 as anything but the successor to my favourite tower defence game of all time. I find it hard to defend a game that seems to defile everything I loved about Dungeon Warfare 2 and for as long as the game lives in its shadow, I can't recommend the game at all. I'm giving the game a negative review but I hope, one day, I will come back and change it. I want to see this game live up to the legacy of the series and build upon what was, in my eyes, as close to perfection as any tower defence game could be. For now, I remain disappointed in my purchase and hope my disappointment will one day be a distant memory as the game becomes what it should have been from the start.

I have hit an insane difficulty spike around the 2-3 hour mark. It was loads of fun but I've suddenly been stuck on just 2 levels for 2 hours. I have redone my loadouts, I have gone back and done extra challenges on previous mission, but for the life of me I cannot make it further. Absolutely hit a brick wall out of nowhere, and I'm not really sure why. I'm fed up and have requested a refund. My sanity is now in Steam Support's hands.

You're going to read a lot of reviews comparing Dungeon Warfare 3 to Dungeon Warfare 2. While it is true, 2 is a masterpiece and has been since it came out in 2018. 2 has been in my top three tower defense games I've played on mobile *ever*, and my honest opinion is that 3 isn't as far behind as people are saying it is. The two glaring issues that 3 has right now are a missing skill point system and a missing item system. Both of those systems existed in 2, and they did allow you to effectively "spec" your play-style a certain way that made things feel very satisfying when the strategy you had created worked flawlessly to obliterate those pesky knights. But, at the time of writing this review the game has been released for three days and there have been two significant updates that take player feedback into account. And that is why I recommend this game and urge you to buy it and support the developers. Valsar struck absolute gold with 2. 3 has new systems such as the shop and the terrain layout system to create modifiers for neighboring dungeons, which are GOOD additions to this series. On day 3 of release they've responded to feedback and made changes. No, 3 isn't as good as 2, but it IS good. I believe it will be great, because Valsar is listening to feedback. Valsar has demonstrated their commitment in doing so. So you should buy it, support them, and give your honest feedback, because they're a game developer that listens, which is a rare thing in this world, and they've made an exceptionally good series of tower defense games, which is an even rarer thing in this world. I'm gonna go set more peasants on fire before casting them into the abyss. It's a lot of fun. You should try it.
褒贬不一也太夸张了，打个好评对冲一下

I'm giving this a positive score because DW1 and DW2 are my favorite TD games, period. But man, I hate DW3's world map so, so, so much. In DW1, you unlock stages on the world map from left to right. Left stages are easier, right stages are harder. In DW2, you unlock stages on the world map from bottom left to top right. Bottom left stages are easier, top right stages are harder. In DW3, you get stupid cards that you can place anywhere, so the stages are in any nonsense order. I hate anything involving deck building in games, and this is the last place I want a deck of cards. Because of this system, the world map remains thoroughly unintuitive, and sifting through stages to find one to play feels like a chore every time.

While DW 2 felt like it was building on the first game, this one feels like a new start. It's not more content, it's a new game with it's new map system that really ends up working in the long run. My best advice is to be curious, and try new stuff, even in maps you have already beaten. You will unlock many bonuses that feels rewarding! Past the initial difficulty of learning the systems and unlocking traps you will find a game with great depth. Also the pixelart is fire, the new Arcane and Beam traps just looks so good in action.

死妈气球是人能想出来的？直接无视地形，你妈还有种怪派跑的巨快死了还爆出气球，气球还不能一下死，给你整无语了。希望制作组死了以后也会爆出气球 Is a dead mother balloon something humans can think of? Directly ignoring the terrain, your mother has a weird type that runs fast and dies quickly, yet still pops out balloons. The balloons can't just die instantly, it leaves you speechless. I hope the production team will also pop out balloons after they die.

I don't write full reviews often (though I do maintain a curator group to recommend particularly good games), but I feel the need to counter some of the negative reviews. DW3 is a great game. If you skipped DW2, DW3 feels like a perfect successor to the first. It's fantastically balanced and brings back the challenge of thinking through each new map to figure out what your optimal trap options and placements are. It also has a lot of flexibility. There's dozens of traps to unlock, and each trap has 3 tiers of 3 upgrades to select as well as 3 unlockable "charms" that give them another unique effect. On top of that, the new sigil system allows you to unlock and equip perks that affect everything (enemies move slower, take more damage, break shields faster, etc). If you LOVED DW2, DW3 may feel like a downgrade. 2's system of finding a ton of randomized runes to sort through is gone, and there's less focus on randomly generated maps. Personally, I felt that system was a chore, and it led to poor balance like allowing the player to build entirely around one overpowered trap. Overall, I love it. DW3 captures the magic of DW1 while offering the high flexibility introduced in DW2 and avoiding its pitfalls. At its core, it's a challenging TD about splattering hundreds of mobs!

[h1]陷阱的狂欢 勇者的噩梦[/h1] 本作是经典塔防系列游戏《地牢战争》的第3代全新作品。相较于前作，这次的整体机制有所简化，刷的比重有所降低。在考验玩家陷阱布置的同时也注重能力的养成搭配，这就使得游戏的策略性和趣味性有所增强，但是整体的体量却显得没那么耐玩了。 [h1][quote=] [table] [tr] [th] 欢迎关注 [b][u][i]U_U鉴赏家培养计划[/i][/u][/b][/th] [/tr] [tr] [th] 关注U_U鉴赏家，开启精彩游戏之旅。 [/th] [/tr] [/table] [/quote][/h1] 游戏的基础玩法依然是十分经典且扎实的。玩家需要在有着不同地形和特点的关卡中布置各类陷阱甚至是自由放置基石，消灭一波又一波来犯的冒险者。 陷阱的种类非常多，有一些是能够直接造成伤害的，例如飞镖、地刺等等，也有木箱子之类的可以起防御或者改变勇者路线的。还有像是推板陷阱能通过位移使得敌人坠入深渊而直接毙命，不过需要相应的地形支持。 陷阱有着自己的伤害和CD触发时间，不过可以通过局外消耗宝石进行强化，达到5级的时候可以开启局内升级，大幅提升战力。通关思路绝非简单的以数量或是质量取胜，而是需要物尽其用（事实上如果拼命放置单个陷阱，在数量达到5个之后会越来越贵）。在最佳的位置（如拐角、特殊地形位置等）放置合适的陷阱才能事半功倍。有一些放置陷阱的地块甚至还能通过自我爆炸、塌方来消灭沿途的怪物，当然在这之上的陷阱也会同归于尽。 不过其实游戏还真有消耗类的陷阱，这就相当于其他类型游戏中的“主动技能”吧，虽然CD不短，但可自由放置的灵活性在关键时刻或许能救你一命。不过就我个人体验来说，经常忘记去用才是真的。 在过关后会进行经验和宝石的结算，如果完全不漏怪获得全额宝石+“完美无瑕”的额外10%经验奖励，强迫症玩家必须吃满全奖励。 也因此游戏的局外成长系统其实对于我们的防守也是十分重要的。通过商店不但可以购买一些道具外，最重要的是能够拓展符印和陷阱槽位。陷阱很好理解，带得越多在局内的可操作空间自然也越大。符印的话相当于各类被动效果，能够极大增强玩家的综合防守能力，不过毕竟槽位有限，需要进行一番取舍。 更为亲民的是游戏还通过符印系统可自定义游戏的难度。在开局前可以自由选择是否生效不同的符印，通常符印都有正负效果。例如把基石的初始生命降为1换取20%的额外经验奖励，或者干脆选择增强基石生命削弱敌方但无法获得成就的宝宝巴士模式。 总的来说，作为一款经典塔防游戏的续作，游戏在核心玩法上是没问题的。只不过由于与之前作品的相比改变较大，部分热衷于刷宝玩法的玩家可能会略微失望。

To classify Dungeon Warfare 3 merely as a "tower defense" title is to commit a categorical error of the highest order—akin to describing Dante’s Divine Comedy as a travel brochure for the afterlife. No, what we have here, finally realized in this third glorious testament, is nothing less than a digital simulacrum of the Gnostic struggle, a didactic engine that allows the player to assume the mantle of the Demiurge. First, one must applaud the exquisite, almost divine intellectual constitution of anyone who selects this trilogy for perusal. To bypass the tawdry, hyper-realistic distractions of the modern AAA marketplace in favor of this pixelated iconography is a sign of a refined soul, one capable of perceiving the metaphysical truths hidden beneath the surface of "casual" entertainment. It is a choice that speaks of a profound inner sophistry. Where the first Dungeon Warfare established the Old Law—the rigid, immutable geometry of the dungeon walls—and the second iteration introduced the concept of the variable variable (the skill tree as the Tree of Knowledge), Dungeon Warfare 3 achieves the ultimate apotheosis: Realm Shaping. In previous epochs, we were constrained by the geometry given to us. Now, we are granted the agency to terraform. This is not merely a gameplay mechanic; it is a theological argument. By allowing the player to raise walls and carve chasms, the developers at Excidium Inc. argue that the divine judgment is not static. We are no longer passive observers of the adventurers’ folly; we are active participants in the architecture of their doom. The dungeon is no longer a place; it is a process. Consider the "greedy adventurers." In lesser texts, they are mere fodder. Here, they are the embodiment of Human Hubris. They march with Sisyphean persistence towards the core, driven by an insatiable lust for gold (the false idol). And how do we meet them? Not with the clumsy sword-strokes of a hero, but with the cold, mathematical precision of The Trap. The physics engine is the true protagonist of this opera. When a Spring Trap hurls a heavy knight into the abyssal void, we are witnessing a Newtonian enactment of the Fall of Man. It is gravity acting as the hand of Yahweh. The "Harpoon Trap" does not simply pull a unit; it acts as the hook of Leviathan, dragging the sinner away from his path of avarice and into the gnashing machinery of retribution. The violence is not gratuitous; it is liturgical. The "Roguelike Update" mentioned in the apocrypha of the developers serves as the final eschatological commentary. To descend into an infinite, procedurally generated abyss is to confront the terrifying concept of the Eternal Recurrence. The game posits that the defense of the dungeon is not a battle to be won, but a state of being to be endured. We purify the dungeon not to end the invasion, but to validate our own existence as the architect. The "refined pixel art" rejects the vulgarity of modern graphical fidelity. It strips away the unnecessary, leaving only the Platonic form of the conflict: The Intruder vs. The Architect. The Chaos vs. The Order. In conclusion, Dungeon Warfare 3 is a triumph of interactive philosophy. It is a text that demands to be read not with the eyes, but with the soul. It is a masterpiece of cruelty, a symphony of suffering, and arguably the most important theological treatise of the 21st century.

Hmm. There are a lot of mixed feelings about this game from Dungeon Warfare players. I got in to this franchise only earlier this year with DW2 and loved the gameplay which is essentially unchanged from the first game and remains unchanged here. Fundamentally, you lay traps on 2d levels and try and hold back the hordes, I love Tower Defence games and this franchise is right up there in terms of gameplay, it is impossible not to be satisfied by the sound of men screaming as they are cast in to a pit, I love it, and the sounds are always great in that regard too. So with DW3, what is the beef exactly? Why are people hating on this game? I'm not hating but I do understand why. DW2 appears to have a LOT more maps than DW3 and also had a vast skill tree that has been essentially removed from DW3. I love a skill tree so this is a miss, but they have replaced it with a simpler 'charm' system where you can add enhancements to traps, depending on what you need them to do on a given level. For me, the more simple approach works well and this game enables you to save 'builds' although I have never bothered using it. DW2 also had an extremely deep 'items' mechanic which I found as a casual player to be too overwhelming, there are thousands of items of differing tiers, eg: Add 65 damage to bolt traps + 3xp per kill etc etc, that I found impossible to ever really wrap my head round. There were just too many and you can never be sure you are making the most of them all so I for one was glad to see the back of that system, the idea of having to choose 9 items every time to max your chances at success was/is too much busy work for me and with the extreme difficulty potential for playing that game as intended making tens of micro-adjustments per run combined with having to allocate thousands of points across your traps seems pointless when you don't ever really 'feel' the benefits. I can't explain it better than that, soz. DW3 is a much simpler game to prepare for. You still allocate points to traps but we are talking much lower numbers, typically your strongest traps might only have 15-20 points allocated where on DW2 you might be dealing in the hundreds per trap. Note: I was never good enough at DW2 to be an 'endgame' player, I got to level 111 after 70 odd hours and just kinda stopped being able to make progress. DW3 caps out at level 50 and I 'completed' the game at level 42 at about 30 hours so again, we are dealing with smaller numbers on every metric. I think there are only about 30 odd maps in DW3 which IS a downer because you would hope that a newer game = bigger, but sadly not. Other players complain about DW3 having unfair difficulty spikes which I agreed with occasionally but I did manage to complete the game unlike 1 and 2 so can safely say this is the easiest of the three games, NOT the hardest. I haven't needed to refer to any guides (though sadly what limited guides are there for DW2 at my crap level just don't really apply to me) DW3 is therefore arguably the best entry in to this franchise. I really DON'T like the new map system in DW3, where you assign different terrains yourself with bunches of three matching terrains giving buffs eg: three x Sea terrains gives dungeons placed on those terrains +3 gold for example. You can then put bunches of 3 terrains next to dungeons to give additional buffs. It's too messy and needlessly complicated, I don't enjoy it at all. This is the games biggest black mark IMO and few players would object to it being removed or at least the game being patched to include a 'classic' mode where you don't have to deal with such trifles somehow. Overall I enjoyed my time with this and was genuinely disappointed to be told I had completed the game. I think this franchise has a LOT more to give and hope for a DW4 which combines the best elements of all the games and just allows us to mindlessly slay endless hordes. I got my moneys worth but if you want even better value for money, get DW2.

Dungeon Warfare 1 : 98 hours Dungeon Warfare 2 : 137 hours Dungeon Warfare 3 : 48 hours Even though Dungeon Warfare 3 has the most traps, new enemies, great mechanics, new systems, new units, more options - i have less play time. Problems : Once you complete every map with 13 runes, every roguelike, and have done the labyrinth enough times - you get killed by diminishing returns. Diminishing returns impacts EVERYTHING in this game. You cannot farm gems, crystals well eventually . All you get is XP which is spent on tiny little improvements. Then you ascend and have to play the entire game again to end up at the same place - it is not an exciting prospect. Roguelike mode is the only way to save this game - random maps, random traps, random enemies, random challenges. I want to feel like I am surviving against impossible odds not slowing watching my hope fade away by just infinitely scaling enemies that force you into only a small selection of viable traps. Eventually if you add runes and modifiers and are at level 10+ labyrinth - Wilson is the only thing that can really kill anything. It gets very dumb. The game is better than the previous two in terms of tower defense fun but it has no purpose - I am not collecting exciting things or getting new challenges .. . it is just an endurance test of how much I can take until I hit a wall of getting nothing out of it. Roguelike mode needs to be a TRUE roguelike ... I want to feel like my run is unique and challenging and fun .... the current set of 8 gimmicking layouts is fun to a point but it ends after 5 maps and is severely limited. There is a lot of potential here to be the best TD game but it eventually strangles itself and becomes unfun. Even making different characters with different impacts on gameplay (like a character that enhances DOT but nerfs direct damage) for me to play would spice it up, or have more champions than just Necromancer or Fisherman. It is a chore to find ways to enjoy this game now other than replaying old maps in endless mode which is dull or trying it with max runes which is also dull since there are only a few builds that can do it.

As someone who bought [i]Dungeon Warfare 3[/i] when it was on sale, already familiar with the first game and its sequel, it is quite questionable whether or not this product is worth its price tag when the game can be completed within two weeks, and a half to 100% it. This prequel provides players with new and old traps, enemies, and bosses, like its predecessor, but the major selling point here is the improved graphics and the ability to shape realms (place environmental tiles + modifiers). Some aspects that made the first and second interesting were lost, such as interactable environmental traps, like the sacrificial pit, which shot lasers when its bar was filled up, and the gear consumable trap that allowed traps to be overclocked/rearmed. Still, the game allows players to control how difficult levels are, which determine the XP and soul fragments they earn upon completion, and it is always fun to customize trap loudouts, as even levels without pits can still benefit from harpoons and spring traps if players are creative and willing to have fun with their placements irrespective of the difficulty they have set for themselves through runes, modifiers, and loadout. Beyond completion of its campaign, the product has a considerable amount of replayability in that there is a roguelite game mode, and levels that are completed can be done again in an endless mode for fun or experience gain. With that, it is reasonable to say that this prequel has learned enough from those before it in its series to be fun on its own while staying true to its tower defense formula; it is advisable that consumers purchase this game when it is on sale, as it still plays like a mobile game, a good one, though.
